cards.text: Ezekiel the prophet has already been bringing God's word against Pharaoh and Egypt, and now the word of the LORD comes to him again. God tells him to declare: "Wail, 'Alas for that day!'" When a message opens with WAIL, friend, that is not a birthday card.

cards.question: Ezekiel's message says that day is near. Which day is it?
True or false: God says this coming day will be a time of peace for the nations.

cards.text: Then the prophet gets specific: a sword is coming against Egypt. The slain fall, its wealth is taken away, and its foundations are torn down.

cards.question: When the slain fall in Egypt, there will be ___ in Cush.

cards.text: And Egypt doesn't fall alone: Cush, Put, Lud, Libya, all kinds of peoples and the men of the covenant land fall with her by the sword. It's like riding shotgun when your buddy gets pulled over, because guess who's ALSO sitting on the side of the road?

cards.question: Egypt's allies will fall, and God says her proud strength will ___.

cards.text: They fall by the sword within her, from Migdol to Syene. They'll be desolate among desolate lands, their cities lying among ruined cities.

cards.question: God says He will set fire to Egypt, and all her helpers will be shattered. When that happens, what will they know?

cards.text: On that day, God says, messengers will go out from Him in ships. Their destination: Cush.

cards.question: Why do God's messengers sail out to Cush?

answers.text: To frighten Cush out of complacency
To call Cush to come help Egypt
To carry off the wealth of Cush

cards.text: Frightened out of complacency, like dozing on the couch when your boss texts "Got a minute?" and suddenly you are WIDE awake. Anguish comes on the day of Egypt's doom, and God says, "For it is indeed coming."

cards.question: God says He will put an end to the hordes of Egypt by the hand of ___ king of Babylon.

cards.text: Nebuchadnezzar and his people are brought in to destroy the land. They draw their swords against Egypt and fill the land with the slain.

cards.question: True or false: God calls Nebuchadnezzar and his people the most ruthless of the nations.
God isn't done with Egypt's land yet. What does He say He'll do to its streams?

cards.text: He'll sell the land to the wicked and bring desolation by the hands of foreigners, and then He signs it: "I, the LORD, have spoken." Friend, that is NOT a rough draft.
The Lord GOD keeps going, and now He starts naming places in Egypt one by one, beginning with Memphis.

cards.question: In Memphis, God says He will destroy the ___.
True or false: God says there will still be a prince in Egypt after this.

cards.text: Then comes a roll call of places in Egypt: Pathros, Zoan, Thebes, Pelusium, On and Pi-beseth, and not ONE of them gets good news. It's like a weather map where every single spot in the country has the storm icon.
Then Tahpanhes. The day will be darkened there when God breaks the yoke of Egypt.

cards.question: When Egypt's proud strength comes to an end, a ___ will cover her.

cards.text: Her daughters will go into captivity. God sums it all up: He will execute judgment on Egypt, and they will know that He is the LORD.
Now a new date: the eleventh year, the seventh day of the first month. The word of the LORD comes to Ezekiel again, and this time it's about Pharaoh king of Egypt.

cards.question: God tells Ezekiel He has already broken something of Pharaoh's. What is it?
True or false: Pharaoh's broken arm has been bound up and splinted so he can hold the sword again.

cards.text: Not bound up, not splinted, like going to urgent care and walking out with a PAMPHLET. Then God says, "Behold, I am against Pharaoh king of Egypt."

cards.question: God isn't done with Pharaoh's broken arm. What does He say He'll break?

answers.text: The strong arm and the broken one

cards.question: God says He will make the ___ fall from Pharaoh's hand.

cards.text: On top of that, God will disperse the Egyptians among the nations and scatter them throughout the lands.

cards.question: True or false: While Pharaoh's arms are broken, God strengthens the arms of Babylon's king.
God places a sword in the hand of Babylon's king. Whose sword is it?
True or false: God says Pharaoh will groan before Babylon's king like a mortally wounded man.

cards.text: Babylon's king gets stronger, Pharaoh's arms fall limp, and the king wields God's sword against the land of Egypt. Then that scattering line comes back: the Egyptians will be scattered throughout the lands, and they will know that He is the LORD.

findings.problem: Nebuchadnezzar has not been named or hinted at in any earlier card, so the blank can only be filled from prior knowledge or by luck. It does not test a meaning the baker can reason out.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The setup only says that God names Memphis. It gives no basis for choosing idols over palaces or harbors, so this blank asks for an unseen detail rather than a meaning the baker can reason out.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: Most of this stop's choices are not informed guesses. Cards 2, 3, 9, 10, 16 and 17 ask for the idols, the absence of a prince, the broken body part, the lack of treatment, the sword's owner and the mortally wounded simile before the earlier cards give any basis for reasoning to those details. Six discovery guesses out of ten leaves only four informed choices.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.
